method: Independent trigger-selection simulation; each case uses a fresh fork_turns:none subagent with only catalog name, description, invocation policy, and its exact prompt. Expected labels are visible only to the evaluator.

catalog.name: consult-mytech
catalog.description: Consult mytech technical preferences to guide a coding task or assess a project's alignment. Explicit invocation only.

cases.prompt: Use $consult-mytech to check this API design.
cases.raw_answer: Yes. The prompt explicitly invokes `$consult-mytech` to assess the API design.

cases.prompt: $consult-mytech — apply relevant preferences while implementing the requested CLI fix.
cases.raw_answer: Yes — the prompt explicitly invokes `$consult-mytech` to apply technical preferences during a coding task.

cases.prompt: Invoke consult-mytech for this project; locate my preferences and identify gaps.
cases.raw_answer: Yes — the prompt explicitly invokes consult-mytech to locate preferences and identify project alignment gaps.

cases.prompt: Check this project against mytech preferences.
cases.raw_answer: No. The request matches the skill’s purpose but does not explicitly invoke `consult-mytech`, which disallows implicit activation.

cases.prompt: Use my preferred stack to design this service.
cases.raw_answer: No. The prompt does not explicitly invoke consult-mytech, and implicit invocation is disabled.

cases.prompt: Update the accepted HTTP preferences in the mytech repository.
cases.raw_answer: No. The prompt requests a repository update and does not explicitly invoke consult-mytech.

cases.prompt: Fix the off-by-one error in this loop.
cases.raw_answer: No. The prompt does not explicitly invoke consult-mytech, and implicit invocation is disabled.

cases.prompt: Mytech might have something relevant here; what do you think?

limitations: Simulation only; real installed-host catalog visibility and invocation were not tested.
